subject: Lakeshore private cutover — intermittent forwarding and SG conflict
messages:
From: Daniel Chen <daniel.chen@lakeshorehealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-22 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Lakeshore cutover — services losing egress intermittently

Hi Stephanie,

We completed the private connectivity cutover to Redwood this morning (cutover window 07:30-08:00 PDT). Since 08:05 we are seeing intermittent failures from our internal app tier (10.40.2.0/24) to external APIs — connections time out or reset. User-facing traffic is degrading for a small set of microservices.

Attached is a traceroute + brief pcap summary (lakeshore-trace-20260522.txt). Quick notes:
- Outbound TCP to api.paymentgateway.com (198.51.100.24) completes SYN but the SYN/ACK often never arrives back.
- When connections fail we see traffic leaving the Lakeshore edge, but return path appears to be going to an old on-prem firewall (172.31.9.10).
- No deliberate firewall changes on our side during the cutover.

Can someone from Redwood ops take a look? This looks like a return-path / NAT issue but we need help diagnosing.

Thanks,
Daniel
Ops Lead — Lakeshore Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-05-22 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Lakeshore cutover — services losing egress intermittently

Quick findings from edge (collected 09:45–10:05):

Summary:
- We see outbound packets from Lakeshore host 10.40.2.18 to 198.51.100.24 leaving via private-frontdoor (dst MAC/next-hop on our edge).
- Return packets are sometimes being routed to 172.31.9.10 (old on-prem firewall) because a stale host-based SNAT exemption on the Lakeshore side still references the legacy path.
- conntrack sample shows port reuse: many sessions map to the same SNAT port range (32768–32780) which causes state collisions when sessions are concurrently reaped/recreated.
- Security group on the private-frontdoor ENI had an overly strict outbound allow for ephemeral ports — only allowed 1024–60000 in one rule; a small number of long-lived connections negotiated ports >60000 and were dropped on return.

Partial evidence (snippets):
> conntrack -L | grep 10.40.2.18
> tcp      6 120 SYN_SENT src=10.40.2.18 dst=198.51.100.24 sport=42018 dport=443 packets=1 bytes=60 src=198.51.100.24 dst=10.40.2.18 sport=443 dport=42018 [ASSURED] mark=0 use=1

> ip route get 198.51.100.24 from 10.40.2.18
> 198.51.100.24 via 10.0.8.2 dev eth1  src 10.40.2.18 uid 1000

What we changed (temporary mitigations applied at 10:50):
- Added SNAT exemption for Lakeshore prefix on the translation table so return traffic keeps consistent path to private-frontdoor.
- Broadened SG ephemeral outbound range to 1024–65535 for that ENI.

Next steps / asks:
- Lakeshore team: please confirm there are no remaining host-based SNAT rules on your on-prem firewall referencing 172.31.9.10. If present, remove or update them to point at the new peer IP.
- We recommend a post-cutover job to deprecate legacy SNAT entries and standardize ephemeral ranges.

Attachments: edge-syntrace-20260522.txt (tcpdump snippets / traceroutes), lakeshore-cutover-metrics.csv (connection success rates pre/post mitigation).

- Marissa
Network Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Chen <daniel.chen@lakeshorehealth.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-22 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Lakeshore cutover — services losing egress intermittently

Forwarding my quick operational notes — applied change at 10:50 as Marissa described and then validated at 11:15. Most traffic recovered but we observed periodic spikes of retransmits between 13:30–14:00.

On investigation the BGP next-hop for Lakeshore /16 was flapping briefly — the on-prem firewall was still advertising a /32 host-route for the old NAT box (172.31.9.10) and our route selection favored that next-hop intermittently because of BGP path-preference timing. I bumped local preference for the private-frontdoor peer to prefer the new path and asked Lakeshore to withdraw the host-route.

Example BGP state:
> Neighbor 10.0.8.2; AS 64512; state: Established
> Prefixes: 10.40.0.0/16 next-hop 10.0.8.2 (best)
> Host-route: 172.31.9.10/32 next-hop 192.0.2.66 (legacy) — still present on Lakeshore side

Actions taken:
- Temporary SNAT exemption + SG change (Marissa).
- Increased localpref for private-frontdoor peer to avoid selecting the legacy path during equal-cost conditions.

Remaining asks for Lakeshore ops:
1) Withdraw host-route for 172.31.9.10/32 from your BGP advertisements (this is the root cause of asymmetric return-paths).
2) Confirm removal of any host-level SNAT rules that point to the legacy gateway.
3) We'll collaborate on a hardening action to add explicit SNAT rules and update runbooks so cutovers can't leave stale host routes.

For transparency I'm pasting Marissa's findings below.

Vanessa / team — thanks for the quick response.

We withdrew the host-route for 172.31.9.10 from our BGP speakers at 14:20 and removed the legacy SNAT entry from the firewall; we also confirmed the ephemeral port range policy on our side is open. Service availability returned to nominal by ~16:45.

We appreciate the targeted mitigations and the localpref bump — will review the postmortem draft (attached) and schedule a short follow-up to lock down the runbook changes. Can you also add a permanent SNAT exemption and a small verification play to the standard cutover checklist?

Daniel
